title: The Voluntary-to-Enforceable Gap: Measuring Commitment Attrition Over Time

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Compelling and critical: quantifying attrition of voluntary commitments directly informs the most pressing governance design question -- whether voluntary approaches work or regulation is needed.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Guided task: cataloguing commitments from documented sources and tracking their status is systematic work suited for guided beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sustained effort: cataloguing all commitments from multiple labs across 2023-2024 and tracking each forward requires thorough but bounded research.

novelty.reasoning: The problem is well-documented journalistically and discussed in policy analysis, but no systematic empirical study catalogues all voluntary AI commitments and quantitatively tracks their attrition over time. The FLI Safety Index provides snapshots, and journalism documents individual cases, but the systematic quantitative attrition measurement is partially novel.

evidence: FLI AI Safety Index (2025) tracks commitment quality across labs but as periodic assessments, not systematic attrition measurement over time
Wildford (2025) 'The promises and perils of voluntary commitments for AI safety' analyzes coordination failure dynamics but as theoretical analysis, not empirical attrition measurement
CNN/AI Business (Feb 2026) documented specific cases of Anthropic and OpenAI weakening commitments, providing journalistic evidence but not systematic quantification
Carnegie Endowment if-then commitments framework (2024) proposes structure for commitments but does not empirically measure attrition rates
EA Forum 'We read every labs safety plan' (2025) provides comparative analysis but not longitudinal attrition tracking
